clue.text: Publication taking on union shows bottle

parts.note: a magazine, shortened to mag, is a publication
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A magazine signing up with a trade union proves it has courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, which is the sense the surface plays on; here it is the large wine bottle. 'Taking on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding twice the standard measure.

clue.text: Carpenter adds piece of moulding (sound) to a barrier

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

indicators.note: the bracketed word tells us the moulding piece is to be taken by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a bead is a narrow rounded strip of moulding

explanation.surface: A woodworker attaches a strip of decorative moulding to a fence or barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The carpenter is a fictional one: the title character of George Eliot's novel, a village carpenter. 'Adds ... to' places the sounded word after A DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of George Eliot's 1859 novel is a carpenter by trade, so the title character fits a capitalised Carpenter.

clue.text: Squiggle perhaps one minor irritant — certain to cover it

indicators.note: one word is to go over, i.e. enclose, the other words named, as a lid covers its contents

parts.note: sure means certain
the Roman numeral I is one
a gnat is a small biting insect, a minor nuisance

explanation.surface: A scribble might be a small annoyance, someone is sure to hide it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the one minor irritant, which SURE covers, giving S + IGNAT + URE.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten autograph is often just a scrawl, so a squiggle is an example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Type of neck fit for woolly

parts.note: a V-neck is a style of neckline on a jumper
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: Choosing a neckline style that suits a woollen jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests knitwear, but 'woolly' means unclear, as in woolly thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly in the sense of muddled or imprecise thinking is a synonym of unclear and hazy.

clue.text: Defender of country has a small group in port

indicators.note: the article and group sit inside the abbreviation for port, between its two letters

parts.note: a trio is a small group of three

explanation.surface: A patriotic defender belongs to a little band stationed in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves and defends their homeland, so is a defender of their country.

clue.text: Monarch to have ties of loyalty — executed soon

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to belong is to be attached by loyalty to a group

explanation.surface: A king or queen demands allegiance, then is put to death before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' is the deletion signal: BELONG loses its head, B, leaving ELONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere long is an archaic phrase for before long, meaning soon.

clue.text: Large architectural construction in timber

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large in clothing sizes
an arch is a curved structure in architecture

explanation.surface: A big building project made out of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch wood is a tough conifer timber used in building and boats.

clue.text: A job to hold Welsh festival in small tree

indicators.note: the job's word holds, contains, the festival's word inside it

parts.note: a task is a job
the Mari Lwyd is a Welsh midwinter folk custom, shortened to Mari

explanation.surface: Someone has the job of hosting a Welsh celebration inside a little tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mari Lwyd is a Welsh New Year folk custom in which a horse's skull on a pole is carried from door to door; 'to hold' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a shrub or small tree with feathery foliage that grows on coasts.

clue.text: Ordained, I'd make to wear fine fabric

indicators.note: a garment worn surrounds its wearer, so the fabric word goes round the others

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton fabric
I'd with the apostrophe dropped
to do is to make, as in do a meal

explanation.surface: A newly ordained priest decides to put on fine linen vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordained' suggests making someone a priest, which the vestments in the surface encourage; here it means decreed, and 'to wear' signals the fabric going round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down a rule is to ordain or decree it, so the past forms match.

clue.text: Criticise one opening for cat flap

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains about putting in a door flap for the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat flap' looks like one phrase; split it: 'flap' is the definition, in the sense of a state of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap means being in a state of agitation or alarm.

clue.text: Express surprise perhaps seafood no longer chokes one

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was

indicators.note: the shellfish word closes round the numeral as if gripping its throat

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish eaten as seafood
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A diner is astonished when an old shellfish dish gets stuck in someone's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, as from surprise, though other emotions also qualify, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Marie Antoinette, say, drinks small amount to relax

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the queen word swallows the measure

parts.note: Marie Antoinette was a French queen, in French a reine
cl is a centilitre, a small amount of liquid

explanation.surface: The French queen sips a little to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Antoinette is an example of a French queen, giving the French word REINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean or lie back, which is a way to relax.

clue.text: Tobacco tin no longer in fashion?

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
out means unfashionable

explanation.surface: Is a tobacco tin now considered unfashionable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snout' is British slang, especially prison slang, for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is slang for tobacco or a cigarette, used chiefly in British prisons.

clue.text: Abandoned out in rain, collapse

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Left outside in the rain, someone falls in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT IN RAIN has the same nine letters as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination means downfall or destruction, a synonym of collapse as a noun.

clue.text: Public official is old in service

indicators.note: the word for old sits inside the church service word

parts.note: Mass is a church service
yore means long ago, olden times

explanation.surface: A civic dignitary is an old hand at church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is only a link; 'in' signals the containment. Mass is the Catholic church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is a woman mayor, the elected civic head of a town.

clue.text: Magistrate's about to arrest a marine commander

indicators.note: arresting means seizing, so the turned word grips the article inside it
about means turned around, so the magistrate's word runs backwards

parts.note: a doge was the chief magistrate of Venice; with the s

explanation.surface: A magistrate is about to detain a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice. 'About' turns the possessive to give SEGOD, and 'to arrest' signals the article caught inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea god such as Neptune rules over the oceans, so commands the sea.

clue.text: Ecstacy,say, is a girl given fur

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl or young woman
a pelt is an animal's fur skin

explanation.surface: Ecstasy is described as a young woman wrapped in fur.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shows itself: the clue writes 'Ecstacy' with a C where the correct spelling has an S, an example of a spelling error.
explanation.definitionFit: The word ecstasy written with a C is a wrongly spelt word, an example of an error in spelling.

clue.text: Silence endlessly serious comic

parts.note: to gag is to silence

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: stern means serious

explanation.surface: A grave comedian refuses to stop silencing people.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a joke-teller, a comedian.

clue.text: Universal god is owned in Sanskrit text

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
Pan is the Greek god of shepherds
had means owned

explanation.surface: A god of all things is held in a Sanskrit scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are ancient Sanskrit philosophical texts of Hinduism.

clue.text: Old editor minuted new motto

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A veteran editor took minutes on a fresh slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus EDITOR plus MINUTED gives the fourteen letters. The answer, French for 'God and my right', is the motto of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase is the motto of the British sovereign, shown on the royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Maureen with struggle to provide entertainment

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Maureen fights to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shown at the cinema is a form of entertainment, an example.

clue.text: Absorb energy, not at first extremely fat

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: gross means extremely fat or bloated

explanation.surface: Take in energy, but not at the start of becoming very obese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' reads as a negation; it gives only N, the first letter of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb someone's full attention.

clue.text: Come into view as some soldiers turn up

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means reading from bottom to top, so both pieces run backwards together

parts.note: eg, for example, can stand for as in 'as in X'
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Something appears as a group of soldiers arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive' but it is the reversal: EGREME read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out and become visible.

clue.text: Formal estimate economist announced, reported herein?

parts.note: a quotation is a formal price estimate

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the economist's name gives the sound of the answer's last word

parts.note: Karl Marx was a political economist

explanation.surface: An economist states an official price estimate in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: reported speech is written inside these marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas enclose words quoted or spoken, so reported words appear within them.

clue.text: Heat for cooking cheaper first from gas and electricity

indicators.note: cooking means altering or messing about, so the letters are rearranged
first from means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: E is a short form for electricity

explanation.surface: Gas and electricity are cheaper for cooking with heat.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAPER rearranges to REPECHA. 'Heat' is a race in a contest, not warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A repechage is an extra qualifying heat that gives losers another chance.

clue.text: Points in lengthy speech made available to view

indicators.note: the compass points go inside the speech word

parts.note: a screed is a long, tedious speech or piece of writing
N and E are points of the compass

explanation.surface: Key points in a long speech are put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' is a common crossword signal for compass letters; 'in' signals the containment, and 'made available to view' means shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A film screened is shown publicly, put up for people to watch.

clue.text: Fish, one dropped from ship almost to the bottom, virtually gutted

indicators.note: in a down clue placing at the bottom means putting the next piece last
almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: an anchor is dropped from a ship

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A fish falls from a ship and sinks nearly to the seabed, almost cleaned out.
explanation.walkthrough: ANCHOR loses its last letter to give ANCHO; 'virtually' gutted gives VY, placed at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy is a small, oily sea fish.

clue.text: Securing horse, I love to get up to break it

indicators.note: breaking into the horse word means the other pieces go inside it

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means reading upwards, so the word for love runs backwards

parts.note: nil, nothing, is love in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Someone catching a horse loves to climb on and break it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love to get up' gives LIN; with I that makes ILIN, which goes into NAG: NA + ILIN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing means fastening or fixing firmly, a synonym of securing.

clue.text: Plane hit by missile — it is scattered at sea

parts.note: a jet is a plane
SAM is a surface-to-air missile

explanation.surface: An aircraft is struck by a missile and its debris strewn over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship, left floating or washed ashore.

clue.text: Table up in diner at last

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the run reads from bottom to top
in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A table is finally set up in the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'dineR AT LAst' lies RATLA, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the communion table in a church.
